person.name: Nephi1
person.title: Son of Lehi1, prophet and founder of Nephites
person.description:
Nephi¹, son of {Lehi|lehi1} and {Sariah|sariah}, was born in [Jerusalem|jerusalem-1] around 615 B.C. and founded the Nephite people. He opens his record by stating he was “born of goodly parents,” taught in his father’s learning, and “highly favored of {the Lord|jesus-christ}” (1 Nephi 1:1). Though young, he was “large in stature,” and after he prayed {the Lord|jesus-christ} softened his heart so that he believed his father’s words and did not rebel as his brothers {Laman|laman1} and {Lemuel|lemuel} did (1 Nephi 2:16).

Sent with his brothers to obtain the brass plates from {Laban|laban} in [Jerusalem|jerusalem-1], Nephi¹ said he would go and do what {the Lord|jesus-christ} commanded, “for I know that {the Lord|jesus-christ} giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way” (1 Nephi 3:7). After two failed attempts, he killed {Laban|laban} with {Laban|laban}’s own sword at the prompting of {the Spirit|holy-spirit} and took the records (1 Nephi 4:18). {The Lord|jesus-christ} told him that if he kept the commandments he would be made “a ruler and a teacher” over his brethren, which set him at odds with {Laman|laman1} and {Lemuel|lemuel} (1 Nephi 2:22).

{The Lord|jesus-christ} commanded Nephi¹ to build a ship to carry the family across the sea to the [promised land|promised-land] (1 Nephi 17:8-9). He built it not after the manner of men but as {the Lord|jesus-christ} showed him; when it was finished his brothers acknowledged the workmanship was fine (1 Nephi 18:1-4). In the [promised land|promised-land] he built a temple modeled on {Solomon|solomon}’s temple, taught his people, and they “lived after the manner of happiness” (2 Nephi 5:16, 27).

Nephi¹ kept two sets of plates: a larger set recording the reign of the kings and the wars of his people, and the smaller set he was commanded to make for an account of the ministry and prophecies, made for a purpose {the Lord|jesus-christ} did not reveal to him (1 Nephi 9:1-6). His record includes a first-person vision of the birth, ministry, and death of {Christ|jesus-christ} and the future of his seed and the {house of Israel|israel} (1 Nephi 11-14). He formally named and set out “the doctrine of {Christ|jesus-christ}” — faith, repentance, baptism, {the Holy Ghost|holy-spirit}, and enduring to the end — and declared it the exclusive path to salvation: “this is the way; and there is none other way nor name given under heaven whereby man can be saved in the kingdom of {God|god}” (2 Nephi 31:2, 21). He closed by calling Jew and all the ends of the earth to believe in {Christ|jesus-christ}, declaring that his words would stand against the unbelieving at the judgment bar (2 Nephi 33:10-15). Later {Nephite|nephites} kings were called second Nephi, third Nephi, and so on, as the people kept his name in remembrance (Jacob 1:11).

person.name: Amalickiahites
person.title: Followers of Amalickiah
person.description:
The Amalickiahites were a faction of Nephite dissenters who followed {Amalickiah|amalickiah} in {his|amalickiah} bid to be made king, active roughly between 73 BC and 65 BC. They were drawn largely from the lower judges of the land, who supported {Amalickiah|amalickiah} after {he|amalickiah} promised to make them rulers over the people, and many of them dissented from the church on the strength of {his|amalickiah} flattering words (Alma 46:1-10).

The group was named when {Moroni|moroni1} rent {his|moroni1} coat to make the title of liberty and prayed for the blessings of liberty on {his|moroni1} people (Alma 46:11-13). The record also notes in the same passage that those who were true believers in Christ took upon them, gladly, the name of Christ, or Christians, in direct contrast to those who had dissented (Alma 46:14-16). {Moroni|moroni1} then sent throughout the land and gathered all who wished to keep their liberty to stand against {Amalickiah|amalickiah} and those who had dissented, who were called Amalickiahites (Alma 46:28). When {Amalickiah|amalickiah} saw that {Moroni|moroni1}’s people were more numerous, and that {his|amalickiah} own people were doubtful about the justice of their cause, {he|amalickiah} took those who would follow {him|amalickiah} and departed into the [land of Nephi|land-of-nephi] (Alma 46:29). {Moroni|moroni1} put to death any of the remaining Amalickiahites who would not enter a covenant to support the cause of freedom, and few refused the covenant (Alma 46:35).

The Amalickiahites who left with their leader are later identified with the {Lamanite armies|lamanites}, who were astonished at the {Nephites|nephites}’ preparation for war (Alma 49:9).

person.name: Corihor1
person.title: Early Jaredite rebel
person.description:
Corihor was a Jaredite, son of King {Kib|kib} and a descendant of {Jared|jared1} through {Orihah|orihah} (Ether 7:3). At thirty-two he rebelled against his father, leaving to dwell in the [land of Nehor|nehor], where he had sons and daughters who became “exceedingly fair,” and he drew away many people after him (Ether 7:4).

After raising an army, Corihor marched against the [land of Moron|moron], where the king dwelt, and took his father captive, which brought to pass {the brother of Jared|jareds-brother}’s saying that the people would be brought into captivity (Ether 7:5). {Kib|kib} remained in captivity under Corihor until he was very old (Ether 7:7).

Corihor’s brother {Shule|shule}, born to {Kib|kib} while still in captivity, made swords of steel from the [hill Ephraim|hill-ephraim], armed his followers, and gave battle to Corihor at the [city of Nehor|nehor], taking the kingdom and restoring it to their father {Kib|kib} (Ether 7:8-9). Corihor later repented of the evils he had done, and {Shule|shule}, now king, gave him power in the kingdom (Ether 7:13).

Corihor had many sons and daughters, among them {Noah|noah2}, who rebelled against {Shule|shule} and against Corihor and drew away his brother {Cohor|cohor1} (Ether 7:14-15). Both {Noah|noah2} and {Cohor|cohor1} are named again, with Corihor, among the fair sons and daughters who did not repent (Ether 13:17).

person.name: Humanity
person.title: The entirety of the human race
person.description:
Humanity, in the Book of Mormon, is the whole progeny of {Adam|adam} and {Eve|eve}. {Lehi|lehi1} taught that the purpose of human existence is joy: “Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy” (2 Nephi 2:25). The Book of Mormon teaches that all humanity was created in {God|god}’s image — {Christ|jesus-christ} told the {brother of Jared|jareds-brother}, “all men were created in the beginning after mine own image” (Ether 3:15-16). By {Adam|adam}’s transgression all mankind became a lost and fallen people, cut off from the presence of {God|god} (Alma 12:22). Each person is free to choose between good and evil, “to choose liberty and eternal life, through the great Mediator of all men, or to choose captivity and death” (2 Nephi 2:27).

The term “men” in the record covers both men and women, and {the Lord|jesus-christ} “esteemeth all flesh in one,” favoring the righteous (1 Nephi 17:35). To overcome the fallen state, a person must be reborn, putting off the natural man and becoming a saint through the atonement of {Christ|jesus-christ} (Mosiah 3:19). {Alma|alma2} asked his congregation, “have ye received his image in your countenances?” and “have ye experienced this mighty change in your hearts?” (Alma 5:14). Salvation comes through no name but {Christ|jesus-christ}’s, and each person’s standing at the last day turns on humbling himself, believing in {Christ|jesus-christ}’s atonement, and submitting to {God|god} (Mosiah 3:17-19).

The record traces a recurring pattern in which the {Nephites|nephites} and {Lamanites|lamanites}, when prospered, harden their hearts and forget {God|god}, and are brought back only through affliction (Helaman 12:1-3). The invitation given to all is to repent, be baptized in {Christ|jesus-christ}’s name, and be sanctified by {the Holy Ghost|holy-spirit} in order to stand spotless at the last day (3 Nephi 27:20).
